purpose: Retrospective evaluation of the pre-existing member-history cap grid against the 2025-2026 calibration drift revealed by the frozen House Journal holdout. Candidate caps and evaluator implementation predate this plan; this run may nominate a shadow candidate but cannot change production defaults.

existingEvaluator.evaluation: Chronological passage-vote member prediction; histories update only after each vote date and are isolated by chamber.

motivation.note: The 2025-2026 House Journal holdout is post-reveal and cannot serve as a new untouched holdout. The pre-existing cap grid is therefore evaluated retrospectively and any winner remains shadow-only until separately validated.

qualifyingConditions: Candidate 2025-2026/house Brier must be lower than uncapped.
Candidate 2025-2026/house expected calibration error must be lower than uncapped.
Candidate 2025-2026/house log loss may not be more than 0.005 worse than uncapped.
Candidate overall Brier may not be more than 0.001 worse than uncapped.
Candidate overall accuracy may not be more than 0.002 lower than uncapped.
Candidate 2021-2022/house Brier and 2023-2024/house Brier may each be at most 0.003 worse than uncapped.
selectionRule.ranking: Among qualifying finite caps, rank by lowest 2025-2026/house Brier, then lowest 2025-2026/house ECE, then smallest finite cap. If none qualify, retain uncapped and record no candidate.
selectionRule.promotionBoundary: A qualifying cap is only a shadow candidate. This retrospective result cannot alter MEMBER_MODEL_VERSION, runtime defaults, production probability calibration, Deep targeting, or Journal mechanics.

guardrails.nextStepIfCandidateQualifies: Replay the nominated cap on the exact frozen 24-case 2025-2026 House cohort and report member Brier/log loss/accuracy, case residuals, and chamber-level expected-Yes error against uncapped. Because the cohort is already revealed, that replay remains descriptive; prospective validation is still required before promotion.
